correctness.rationale: The multiplier is explicitly paired into a weighted sine kernel. A finite geometric-series derivative identity gives \(2\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(1-k/n)\sin(kt)=(\sin t-n^{-1}\sin(nt))/(1-\cos t)\). On the critical \(t=\pi r/n\) grid, \(\sin(nt)=0\), yielding the cotangent samples away from the two points where the original sine sum is exactly zero. The normalized absolute kernel mass is the endpoint convolution norm and is attained by a sign witness; duality gives the \(\ell^1\) endpoint. Parity splitting proves the exact two-scale identity. After subtracting \(2/(\pi x)\), Euler--Maclaurin and the harmonic-number expansion give the stated asymptotic and the coefficient \(-\pi/36\). The packaged verifier independently checks the finite identities; it is corroborative rather than the proof.

value.rationale: Conjugate Fejér means are a canonical regularization of conjugate Fourier/Hilbert summation, and their endpoint convolution norm is the exact worst-case stability factor. The result is an all-n structural theorem at the natural critical sampling rate, not a fixed-size computation. The exact parity decomposition connects the smoothed constant to the unsmoothed cyclic Hilbert constant, while the asymptotic gives both the logarithmic growth and the first finite-size correction.
